attributes.method: Every probe replays the TU's OWN shipped ninja command line, parsed out of build.ninja, and is FIDELITY-GATED: the unmodified replay must be BYTE-IDENTICAL to build/GUNE5D/src/**/.postprocess/body/<unit>.o before any variant result from that TU is trusted. 12 of 12 representative TUs passed that gate. Scoring is against the dtk-extracted target object on RAW compiler output, never the WebFrank-postprocessed object.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: No compiler version in build/compilers and no point in the mwcc option space reproduces the WebFrank-pinned targets from our existing source. MEASURED 2026-09-01 over 11 representative TUs spanning every rule class of claim.CV_webfrank-rule-class-taxonomy.20260901.v1, 56 variants each (616 variant compiles, 591 successful). AXES SWEPT, all on top of each TU's exact shipped cflags: the full -opt keyword vocabulary the 1.2.5n binary itself reports (off/on/all, [no]space, [no]speed, level=1..3, [no]cse, [no]deadcode, [no]deadstore, [no]lifetimes, [no]loopinvariants, [no]propagation, [no]strength, [no]dead, [no]peephole, [no]schedule, [no]functions), -schedule on|off, the full -inline vocabulary (on|smart, none|off, auto, noauto, all, deferred, level=1..3), -func_align 4|8|16|32, and 22 archive compiler versions (GC 1.0, 1.1, 1.1p1, 1.2.5, 1.2.5n, 1.3, 1.3.2, 1.3.2r, 2.0, 2.0p1, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 3.0a3, 3.0a3.2/.3/.4, 3.0a3p1, 3.0a5, 3.0a5.2, Wii 1.0/1.1/1.3). RESULT: ZERO variants reduced any pinned function to a byte-shape match, and only three variants improved a TU's aggregate score at all (-opt nolifetimes on mempool, -opt nopropagation on controls and mb_particle), each of which broke at least one currently-STRICT sibling in the same TU. TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS worth keeping. (1) The scheduler axis is SATURATED, not unexplored: although mwcc documents `-schedule on|off; default is off`, the shipped -O4 line already schedules, so `-schedule on` and `-opt schedule` are exact no-ops against the baseline while `-schedule off`/`-opt noschedule` destroy the match (sysservice::sysPollResetButton 2 -> 18 differing words, audio.c aggregate 24 -> 114). No permutation-class residual is a missing-scheduler artifact. (2) The recolor residual is INVARIANT under the entire option space: sysservice::sysClearFlags (4 differing words, a single r4->r0 rename) scored exactly 4 under all 54 variants that compiled, including every compiler revision from 1.0 to Wii/1.3. ONE POSITIVE CONTROL proves the sweep can detect a win and identifies the true variable: mb_particle::getSinCos, a pure FPR recoloring of 14 words with no structural difference, IS reproduced byte-exactly by GC/3.0a3 and GC/3.0a5.2 under the identical cflags, while GC/1.2.5, 1.3 and 2.7 all produce our (wrong) colouring. That is a register-ALLOCATOR revision boundary, and it comes at the documented melee price: those versions break 33 of the 39 currently-strict functions in the same TU. POPULATION-SCALE CONFIRMATION (tools/gdl/composed_census/cv_probe.py + the mw_population driver, same fidelity gate applied per TU): every TU holding a pure-family residual was recompiled under all 22 archive versions with its own shipped cflags. 104 pure-family functions (RECOLOR / PERMUTE / LIVEZERO / LIVEZERO+RECOLOR) were tested; EXACTLY ONE is reproduced by any version — mb_particle::getSinCos, by the GC/3.0a3 and GC/3.0a5 families. The per-version ledger over that subset, exact functions GAINED vs currently-strict functions BROKEN: GC/1.0 0/9, GC/1.1 0/1, GC/1.1p1 0/771, GC/1.2.5 0/1, GC/1.2.5n 0/108, GC/1.3 0/862, GC/1.3.2 and 1.3.2r 0/856, GC/2.0 through 2.7 0/856, GC/3.0a3 through 3.0a5.2 1/898, Wii/1.0-1.3 0/886. The best possible compiler swap in the archive therefore trades 898 exact functions for 1. Note also that GC/1.0 and GC/1.1 are nearly codegen-identical to 1.2.5 on this code (9 and 1 strict functions changed) and still gain nothing, so the target's colouring is not a near-neighbour revision either. CONSEQUENCE: the pinned residual classes are attributable to allocator/scheduler variance under a compiler revision we do not hold, exactly as the postprocessor class ceiling requires -- and swapping to any compiler we DO hold is a strict loss. Do not re-run a compiler-or-flag sweep on a recolor, permutation, or live-zero residual; cite this record instead. Scope note: this supersedes nothing but extends the 2026-07 walls flagsweep result (tools/gdl/flagsweep.py docstring: no parked residual moved under any variant), which used a 27-entry battery on parked walls before the pinned population existed.
